Build a **per-user credential layer for shared MCP servers**: an admin configures one server template, while each user securely supplies their own API key, with secrets injected only into approved headers or URL paths. That targets a concrete multi-user workflow: avoiding shared keys, duplicate server configs, or a custom proxy.

The strongest evidence is an [open Open WebUI feature request](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/issues/19313): its author asks for personal credentials on a globally configured MCP server, and another commenter describes using separate configurations or a proxy for users’ individual Pappers API keys. The group has **2 distinct requesters in the last 365 days**, an **Early** signal, not proof of market size or willingness to pay. I also reviewed requests about real-device Playwright testing and Discord event webhooks; those are narrower, similarly early asks. GitHub requests may be feature requests rather than buying intent.

A useful first test: interview multi-user Open WebUI admins about how they currently handle MCP credentials and whether that workaround is painful enough to replace.
